Stock Chart of the Week: Lennar breaks higher, but $85 is the next big test

What I find particularly interesting about the latest stock market rotation is that opportunities may be emerging even within sectors that have recently underperformed.

Lennar Corporation (NYSE: LEN) provides a good example.

While the broader consumer discretionary sector has struggled, Lennar, one of America's largest homebuilders, has staged a significant recovery following a difficult period after its September earnings.

On Thursday, October 22, LEN surged 8.69%, breaking above the declining price channel that had contained its shares since August. Friday's close at $84.92 preserved the breakout, bringing the two-session advance to approximately 9.3%.

The move becomes even more interesting when compared with the broader sector.

Lennar is outperforming its sector by almost 10 percentage points

Between the October 21 and October 23 closes:

  • Lennar (LEN): +9.29%

  • Equal-weight consumer discretionary ETF (RSPD): -0.57%

  • LEN outperformance: +9.86 percentage points

This is noteworthy because Lennar advanced sharply while the broader consumer discretionary benchmark declined.

The stock has also recovered approximately 18.3% from its October 14 intraday low of $71.78.

That does not prove a lasting bullish reversal, but it does suggest that Lennar's recent price behavior is becoming more constructive.

Sometimes the most interesting candidates are not found in the strongest sectors. They are stocks beginning to show strength while their broader sector remains under pressure.

Why $85 could be important for Lennar shares

The accompanying daily chart shows that LEN has broken above its declining channel and returned to a previously important trading area.

Around $85 lies the approximate point of control from its earlier earnings-period trading range. This represents the price at which the greatest trading volume occurred during that historical period.

Such areas can attract renewed attention from buyers and sellers because considerable trading previously took place there. However, they do not guarantee that prices will move toward or away from them.

LEN reached $85.21 during Friday's session before closing at $84.92, just below that reference.

Three areas deserve attention:

Around $85: The immediate test

A daily close above $85, followed by sustained trading or a successful retest, would strengthen the case that buyers are regaining control. Repeated failures around this level could indicate that overhead selling pressure remains significant.

Around $81-$82: The first important support area

If the stock pulls back, this area could help determine whether the recent breakout is sustainable. A successful recovery from this zone would support the bullish interpretation. Sustained trading below it would weaken the recovery case.

Around $90: The next potential upside reference

If buyers establish acceptance above $85, the previous trading area's upper boundary near $90 becomes a relevant reference. It is not a guaranteed target, and the stock would still need to overcome selling pressure along the way.

A more substantial retreat toward $77-$78 would suggest that much of the recent improvement has been lost.

Does Lennar's business outlook support a recovery?

This is where investors need to distinguish between improving share-price behavior and improving company fundamentals.

Lennar's September 16 earnings report showed that its third-quarter new home orders declined 9% year over year, while deliveries fell 3%. The company reported a 15.8% gross margin on home sales and diluted earnings of $1.19 per share.

Those figures illustrate why the investment case is not straightforward.

Mortgage rates, housing affordability and builder incentives remain important influences on demand and profitability.

A decline in mortgage rates could make new homes more affordable and potentially support demand. But investors should also examine whether Lennar can maintain margins without relying excessively on discounts and financing incentives.

The next useful fundamental questions are whether new orders begin recovering, gross margins stabilize and management demonstrates improving profitability.

A technically convincing breakout would become more persuasive as a longer-term investment thesis if those business fundamentals also improved.

What would change the bullish interpretation?

There is a credible opposing argument: Lennar may simply be experiencing a powerful rebound within a previously damaged trend.

The stock remains below earlier trading levels, and two strong sessions cannot establish a durable multi-month recovery.

A failure to hold above the recently reclaimed trading area, especially if accompanied by renewed weakness across homebuilders, would challenge the emerging bullish case.

Conversely, continued relative strength, sustained trading above $85 and improving housing-market fundamentals would provide stronger reasons to investigate the stock further.

The lesson from Lennar and sector rotation

What I find especially interesting is not merely that LEN has rallied almost 9.3% in two trading sessions.

It is that the stock has started behaving differently from its broader sector, breaking a declining technical pattern and recovering important historical trading prices while consumer discretionary shares remain under pressure.

This is precisely why sector analysis should be a starting point rather than the final word when selecting stocks.

A weak sector can contain emerging leaders, just as a strong sector can contain vulnerable companies.

Lennar has achieved an encouraging first step by breaking out of its declining channel. The next test is whether buyers can establish and maintain control around $85. That distinction could help determine whether the recovery deserves increasing attention or remains another temporary rebound.

For now, LEN is a stock worth investigating further, not an automatic buy, at your discretion. item.title: NZDUSD buyers are trying to make a play. The 38.2% retracement remains the next hurdle.
item.description:
The NZDUSD has moved higher on four of five trading days this week, giving buyers something to build on after a sharp decline from the August high. The recovery has included a failed break below the rising 100-hour moving average and two successful tests of that moving average today.

Those are encouraging developments for the buyers. They are starting to show up on dips and defend a technical level.

However, there is still work to do. The price remains below the 38.2% retracement of the August-to-October decline. Until that level is broken, the move higher remains a relatively modest correction within the broader move lower.

A 422-pip decline left buyers with a hill to climb

From the August 21 high near 0.5986 to the October 14 low near 0.5564, the NZDUSD fell 422 pips, or 7.05%.

That was a sizable move. Sellers controlled the trend, and rallies along the way gave them opportunities to sell at higher levels.

The buying started to gain more traction on October 16. Since then, the price has worked higher, moving back above its hourly moving averages and putting some distance between the current price and the October low.

The question now is whether the buyers can turn that initial recovery into something more meaningful. To do that, they need to keep holding support below and start breaking resistance above.

Sellers had their shot below the 100-hour MA

Yesterday’s correction lower (only decline over the last 4 trading days), took the price back below the rising 100-hour moving average. That gave sellers an opportunity to regain more control and interrupt the recovery.

They could not sustain the break.

Instead, the price snapped back above the moving average. Sellers had their shot and missed.

Today, the price returned to the 100-hour MA twice, and both tests found buyers. That helps establish the moving average as a level traders are watching and leaning against.

The 100-hour MA is near 0.56835 and rising. Stay above it, and the short-term bias remains more bullish. Buyers have a technical reason to stay involved and a nearby reference for defining their risk.

The nearby swing area adds to the support

The moving average also sits within a swing area between 0.56736 and 0.56860.

That combination makes this an important support region. Buyers would prefer to keep the price above the rising 100-hour MA. If the price slips below it, the bottom of the swing area at 0.56736 becomes the next test.

A sustained move below both would weaken the recovery and give sellers more confidence. The 200-hour MA near 0.56553 would then become another downside reference.

For now, however, today’s repeated holds at the 100-hour MA show buyers continuing to defend their position.

The 38.2% retracement is the next hurdle

On the topside, the next key target is the 38.2% retracement at 0.57258.

I like to see the 38.2% retracement reached and broken as a minimum correction of a trend move. It helps show that buyers can take back a meaningful portion of the decline.

The NZDUSD has not cleared that hurdle yet.

Holding support is one part of the recovery. Breaking resistance is the next. A move above 0.57258—and the ability to stay above it—would strengthen the buyers’ case and open the door for the next push higher.

The 50% midpoint lines up with an old swing area

Above the 38.2% retracement, attention turns toward the 0.5761–0.5777 swing area.

That region has several historical turning points on the chart. The 50% midpoint at 0.57756 also sits near the upper end of the area, giving traders another technical reason to focus on it.

Getting there would take back roughly half of the August-to-October decline. It would also bring the price into a region where sellers could look to lean against resistance.

There are steps to take before that happens. The buyers are making a play, and this week’s price action is giving them some encouragement. Now they need to keep the 100-hour MA underneath them and get through 0.57258 to keep the climb going.

item.title: US expected to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian products as soon as today - report
item.description:
Election season is doing what trade negotiators couldn’t.

The Wall Street Journal reports the US is preparing to lift 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, with a proclamation possibly coming as soon as today. The motivation is political: Maine Sen. Susan Collins has been lobbying for relief and is in a dead heat with Democrat Troy Jackson with less than two weeks to go until Election Day.

Unfortunately, there is no real sign of a political thaw here as Trump could also raise other tariffs. USD/CAD is dow n18 pips to 1.3990 today and unmoved on this report.

The details:

  • Scope and timing could still change, according to the WSJ’s sources
  • The cuts may be offset by higher tariffs on other Canadian goods
  • The White House says any announcement will come from the administration and calls the reports speculation
  • USTR declined to comment

This would be the second adjustment to the 50% tariffs. Last month, Washington exempted road salt and cement and added other products to keep the affected total at about $20 billion, or roughly 5% of Canadian exports to the US. Collins took credit for that change on the campaign trail. Jackson’s reply in their debate was that Mainers “can’t eat road salt.” Food and lumber are a different matter.

The politics go well beyond Maine. In Michigan, GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers is now running ads urging Trump to end the trade war with Canada after spending months backing it. In New Hampshire, John Sununu has also criticized the Canada tariffs.

For background, Trump imposed the 50% levies in late August after last-minute talks broke down. He used Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, the Smoot-Hawley provision, which had never been used before. Canada retaliated, Trump responded with import bans on some Canadian products, and he has threatened to double tariffs on Canadian autos in January if there’s no deal. A New Jersey food importer filed suit this week arguing Section 338 goes beyond the administration’s authority.

Again, I don't see this as a thaw. It’s a swap and the dollar value covered stays around $20 billion and the headline effect for Canada is mostly reshuffling. At the same time, if he wanted real political gains for Republicans before the midterms, he could drop the tariffs altogether and make a deal.

Update: The announcement came from Collins, who noted several products: blueberry, potoatos, apple and seaweed among them.

  • Before the open: Caterpillar, Carrier, Eli Lilly, Vulcan Materials, STMicroelectronics and L3Harris.

  • After the close:Amazon, Intel, Sandisk, Roblox, Reddit, Twilio, Coinbase, Starbucks and Rivian.

Caterpillar offers a window into equipment demand and business investment. After the close, Amazon leads a wide-ranging group covering chips, consumer spending, digital advertising and cryptocurrency trading.

Friday, October 30

  • Before the open: Exxon Mobil, Chevron, BP, Regeneron, AstraZeneca, and General Dynamics.

Energy takes a prominent role to finish the week, with traders watching production, margins, spending plans and management’s outlook.

Watch the reaction as closely as the results

An earnings beat does not automatically mean a stock moves higher. Expectations matter. Guidance matters. So does what has already been priced in (watch the technicals for clues on what is priced in).

If companies deliver good numbers and their shares cannot rally—or an early rally quickly fades—that tells traders something about the appetite to buy. Conversely, disappointing results followed by a recovery can signal that sellers had their shot and could not keep control.

For the broader technology market, the technical roadmap is clear. Get above the 100-day moving averages and stay above, and the buyers improve their position. Stay below, and the sellers retain the advantage, with the 200-day moving averages waiting underneath.

The earnings will provide the headlines. The price action will tell us what traders think of them.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

French bonds stand out for the week

France remains the standout. Its 10-year yield fell 6.2 basis points today to 5.018%, providing some relief, but that did little to reverse the weekly increase.

item.title: US stocks are mixed, but weak breadth keeps the recovery in question
item.description:
The four major US stock indices are telling different stories today. The Dow industrial average is under the most pressure, the S&P 500 is modestly lower, and the Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq 100 are trading higher.

Here is the snapshot:

  • Dow industrial average: Down 473.64 points, or 0.90%, at 52,394.34.

  • S&P 500: Down 10.18 points, or 0.13%, at 7,653.25.

  • Nasdaq Composite: Up 57.33 points, or 0.22%, at 26,066.19.

  • Nasdaq 100: Up 133.19 points, or 0.46%, at 29,091.88.

However, look underneath those headline numbers and the picture is less encouraging. Declining stocks outnumber advancing stocks across all four indices—even in the two Nasdaq indices that are trading higher.

Within the Dow, just five stocks are higher versus 25 lower. In the S&P 500, there are 147 advancers versus 336 decliners. The Nasdaq 100 has 44 stocks advancing versus 56 declining, while the Nasdaq Composite has 1,183 advancers versus 1,827 decliners.

That tells traders the buying is selective. The Nasdaq indices are getting enough support from their more influential stocks to keep the headline readings positive, but the gains are not being shared across the market.

The sector breadth reinforces that caution. Energy stands out with 19 stocks advancing and just one declining. Technology is more balanced at 28 versus 26. Financials, healthcare, industrials and utilities all show considerably more decliners than advancers.

So what does that mean for traders?

The positive Nasdaq readings give buyers something to work with. But can they build on those gains? Can the S&P turn higher and the Dow find support? Or will the weak breadth eventually drag the Nasdaq indices back down?

For me, the technicals help define those answers. A bounce is a start. Getting above resistance—and staying above—is what gives buyers more control. Hold below those levels, and sellers can still lean against them.

In the video, I take a look at the Dow industrial average, S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq 100, outlining the key technical levels in play, why they matter, and what buyers and sellers need to do next.

item.title: AUDUSD recovery runs into the 100-day moving average. What next?
item.description:
The AUDUSD has found support and resistance against two separate moving averages. They are providing the borderlines for both buyers and sellers now. 

The low for the week was on Monday.

Recall, that the AUDUSD has worked its way higher from Monday’s low near 0.6970, with buyers pushing back above a familiar swing area between 0.6989 and 0.6994.

That area is marked by the red numbered circles on the chart. The repeated highs and reactions tell traders why it matters. What had been a ceiling needed to be broken to give the buyers more control. Once above, that ceiling becomes a potential floor.

The break higher opened the door for a move toward the next key target: the 100-day moving average at 0.7032.

The buyers made their move. But at that moving average, the sellers showed up.

Sellers lean against the 100-day MA

On Wednesday, the price tested the 100-day moving average and stalled. Today, sellers leaned against that level again.

Why sell there? It gives traders a clear level to define and limit risk. Stay below, and the sellers can look for a rotation lower. Move above and stay above, and that bearish trade loses some of its technical support.

A sustained break above 0.7032 would have traders looking toward:

  • 0.70447: An intervening chart level.

  • 0.70506: The 200-day moving average.

  • 0.70654: The 50% midpoint of the September-to-October decline.

Getting above the 100-day MA would be another step forward for the buyers. They would still have work to do, however, with the 200-day MA waiting above.

Buyers defend the 100-hour MA below

While sellers have defended resistance, buyers have also been leaning against support.

Pullbacks on Thursday and Friday stalled near the 100-hour moving average, currently around 0.7008. That makes it a close risk-defining level for buyers looking for the recovery to continue.

Stay above is more bullish. Break below, and the door opens for a rotation back toward:

  • 0.6989–0.6994: The swing area marked by the red numbered circles.

  • 0.6984: The rising 200-hour moving average.

A move back below those levels would take away more of the buyers’ progress from earlier this week.

For now, the battle is defined. Sellers are leaning against the 100-day MA above. Buyers are leaning against the 100-hour MA below. Traders are waiting for the next shove.

In the video, I walk through those levels, explain why they matter, and outline what buyers and sellers need to do to take more control.
